{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine_of_Italy|Cuisine of Italy]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian_cuisine|Vegetarian cuisine]]

This article describes general preparation procedures for the popular Italian appetizer (or ''antipasto'') '''Bruschetta''' (plural ''bruschette''), slices of toasted or grilled bread rubbed with garlic, drizzled with olive oil, and seasoned with salt and pepper.<ref name=Field>{{cite book |last=Field |first=Carol |title=Italy in Small Bites |publisher=William Morrow and Company, Inc. |location=New York, New York |date=1993 |page=77 }}</ref> This basic preparation is frequently topped with combinations of flavorful seasonal ingredients. It is a dish coming from the Southern Italian culinary tradition, though variants exist throughout Italy. It is commonly mispronounced in America as "bru-shetta", but should be pronounced with a hard K sound, "bru-sketta."

There are many types of ''bruschetta'', some involving special roasted and/or hard bread which may require a different preparation than the one below. 

The recipe below is a meeting point between Northern and Southern Italy, using an Italian or French baguette-style loaf. You can adapt this recipe to as many servings as you need. As a guideline, you can serve 1 or 2 ''bruschette'' per person.

== Ingredients ==

=== Base ===
* 1 loaf of Italian or French [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]], sliced ½ inch (1.25 cm) thick on the bias
* ½ head [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* Kosher salt or sea [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* Freshly-ground black [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* Extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive oil|olive oil]]
* Toppings of your choice (see examples below)

=== Toppings ===

* Chopped [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] with [[Cookbook:Arugula|arugula]] or [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]]
* Cooked white [[Cookbook:Beans|beans]] (topped, if you like, with sautéed kale)
* Sautéed [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]] (preferably wild varieties)
* Minced [[Cookbook:Anchovy|anchovies]] flavored with wine [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] and herbs
* Thinly-sliced [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]] crisped under the [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]]
* Pugliese-style chopped mixture of summer vegetables (red [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]], [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]], flat-leaf [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]], and [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|red pepper flakes]])

==Procedure==
#Toast the bread slices in a toaster oven, under a broiler, or on a grill, until they turn golden.
#Immediately rub the bread with the cut side of the garlic. Sprinkle with salt and black pepper, and drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
#Serve warm topped with whatever combinations of seasonal ingredients you choose.<ref name=Field></ref>
